Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai

Subject: Marketplace SKU tier harmonization & reseller margin evidence for HumberTech private offer

Hi Lisa —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation, I’m sending a first pass at a private-offer SKU mapping and the margin split mechanics we typically use when a reseller is involved. I’ve attached the SKU workbook (humber_private_offer_SKUs.xlsx) and a supporting margin calc (humber_margin_calc_v2.csv).

Quick summary of the ask from your side:
- Confirm which SKU families you want listed in the GCP and Azure marketplace entries (we included the three you mentioned: compute-core, inference-lite, and inference-pro).
- Verify whether HumberTech will act as reseller (pass-through) or end-customer billing. That affects how we display the list price vs. netback.
- Provide any procurement evidence template you need for PO/legal review (we’ll push MSA redlines separately).

Our proposal (high level):
1) Tier A (commit >= $250k/yr): 20% reseller margin, list price anchored 12% above net price to preserve marketplace comparables.
2) Tier B (commit 100–250k/yr): 15% reseller margin, modest list price uplift to cover marketplace fees.
3) Tier C (pilot & evaluation <100k/yr): 8% reseller margin, flat list price to avoid blocking trials.

Notes: these are negotiable — I’d like to understand whether HumberTech needs accelerated credits, retroactive true-ups, or invoice-path constraints.

Next steps: can we get the procurement contact and typical PO cadence? I’m proposing a short call early next week to align SKUs and finalize the PO-ready package.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0198

Appreciate the summary and the files. Procurement is looped on this thread (procurement@humbertech.com) — they’ll need the detailed margin evidence and our Tax/Invoice preferences. Two quick items from my side:
1) HumberTech will act as reseller in AP/EMEA for this pilot but requires pass-through invoice path into our ERP (we use Coupa).
2) We prefer a three-tier commit structure but our finance team historically asks for explicit examples of netback calculations per SKU — can you include line-item netback (USD) for a sample monthly run-rate?

I’ll coordinate internally to get a procurement lead and confirm a PO cadence (weekly/biweekly cycles). Proposed call next Tue (10th) at 10am ET? If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite.

Subject: RE: Marketplace SKU tier harmonization & reseller margin evidence for HumberTech private offer

Internal —

I opened the margin workbook and added a conservative netback tab (see humber_margin_calc_v2.csv). Key assumptions I used: marketplace seller fee = 9.5% for GCP/Azure, estimated tax and transactional fees = 2.3%, and overhead allocation = 1.2%.

Practical recommendations:
- Use a 3-tier list price anchor (naomi’s proposal) but show both list price and customer-facing discounted price in the SKU doc — this helps procurement reconcile marketplace listing vs. reseller invoice.
- For Tier A, offer an onboarding credit equivalent to one month at 10% of committed run-rate to accelerate usage; finance is usually ok if committed ARR threshold is met.
- Include a line in the SKU workbook that explicitly states the invoice path (Redwood -> HumberTech -> End Customer) and an alternate flow (Redwood -> End Customer) for pilot accounts.

I’ve also flagged the MSA redline that legal will want (sending separately): main ask is to confirm the audit/evidence window for channel credits (we generally ask 90 days).

Ben
Director, Channel Sales Operations
